claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I'm eligible for Child Benefit. I'm asking about my one child, Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about Child Benefit for your one child, Alex.

To assess eligibility, I need to gather some details about your situation. Let me start with the first question:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 10 years old - he was born in 2014.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So Alex was born in 2014 and is currently 10 years old.

**Are you the parent or guardian of Alex, and do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I am Alex's parent, and I do live in the UK, but Alex doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

**Can you tell me more about Alex's current living situation? Specifically, who does Alex live with at the moment, and for how long has this arrangement been in place?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his mum. This arrangement has been in place for a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. I understand Alex lives with his mum.

**Are you Alex's father, or are you his mother?** This will help me understand the household arrangement better.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So you're Alex's dad, and Alex currently lives with his mum in the UK.

**Is Alex's mum already receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or are you aware of whether she has claimed it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if she's claimed it or not, to be honest.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's understandable. Let me ask another question to help clarify the situation:

**Are you the person who is primarily responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and upbringing, or is that responsibility with Alex's mum?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex's mum is the one who has the day-to-day responsibility for him since he lives with her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's an important factor.

**Do you provide any financial support for Alex, such as maintenance payments or child support to Alex's mum?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards things for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that you provide financial support for Alex.

I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit. Let me explain the situation:

Based on the UK Child Benefit rules, Child Benefit is typically paid to the person who is **responsible for the day-to-day care of the child**. In Alex's case, since Alex lives with his mum and she has the primary day-to-day responsibility for his care, she would be the person entitled to claim Child Benefit for him.

As Alex's father who doesn't live with him and isn't responsible for his day-to-day care, even though you do provide financial support, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex yourself.

However, if Alex's mum has not already claimed Child Benefit for Alex, she should do so as she meets the eligibility criteria as the person with day-to-day responsibility for him.
